title: The Canticle, whole (Francis)
hookLine: sun, moon, wind, water, fire, earth, and death, all praising
tomorrow: what comes first: doing something, or looking?

lines: THE WORD NOBODY SAYS AT DINNER.
cards: Some families can't say the word death at the dinner table. Others plan the funeral songs over dessert. Most of us sit somewhere in between, changing the subject.

Francis of Assisi wrote a song that names death out loud and calls her Sister: Sister Bodily Death, whom no living person can escape. And he says it kindly, as one more voice in a long praise of everything God made.

teach.b: It's the Canticle of the Creatures, in Francis's own Italian dialect, not in Latin. First, the opening. Most high, almighty, good Lord: praise, glory, honor and blessing belong to you.
Then the refrain begins: Laudato si', mi' Signore, praised be you, my Lord. Second, the sky. Brother Sun, who brings the day and is radiant, carries your likeness, Francis says.
Sister Moon and the stars, clear and precious and beautiful. Brother Wind, and air and cloud and every kind of weather. Third, the ground.
Sister Water, useful, humble, precious and pure. Brother Fire, who lights the night, cheerful and strong.
Sister our Mother Earth, who feeds and rules us, with her fruits and colored flowers and herbs. Fourth, the people and the end. Praise for those who forgive for love and bear trouble in peace.
Tradition says Francis added those last verses later, the death verse near the end of his own life. He doesn't make death an enemy.
He gives her a place in the family, and the song closes: praise and bless my Lord, give thanks, and serve him with great humility.
For a family facing it this week, that's what the song offers: a way to say the word without running.

how: Catholics sing the Canticle in many hymn versions, and Pope Francis took its refrain, Laudato si', as the title of an encyclical on care for creation.

o: Francis's song of all creation praising God
a list of animals Francis tamed and blessed
a chant monks sing at the hour of sunrise

s: the Canticle is a nature poem that never mentions death
near the end Francis praises God for Sister Bodily Death.
Francis wrote it in his own Italian dialect, not in Latin
its refrain is Laudato si', mi' Signore: praised be you, my Lord.
Francis calls the sun Mother Sun
it's Brother Sun. the earth is Sister our Mother Earth.

games.q: a friend's grandpa is in hospice, and her family won't say the word. she asks how Francis would talk about it. what's closest?
o: name it gently, as part of the family God made.
never say it; hope means not naming it at all.
call it the enemy, and fight it to the very end.
games.why: Francis gave death a verse and a name, Sister Bodily Death, inside a song of praise. not an enemy, not a secret: one more member of creation's family.

practice: Step outside if you can, or open a window. Listen for one sound at a time, a breath each: wind, water, a bird, a voice, your own feet on the earth.
If you know the Canticle, pray it whole out there; otherwise, simply call each sound brother or sister as it comes.

wordCard.voice: The Canticle. Francis's song where sun, moon, wind, water, fire, earth and even death are family, and all of them praising.

orig.note: Umbrian Italian, not Latin: praised be you, the refrain of Francis's canticle.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: all creation praising, even the sister nobody invites to dinner. Until next time.
